sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Intermediate Application (8–14)

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the orchestra hall, $\begin{cases}6x+y=-3\\18x+ky=7\end{cases}$ For what value of $k$ does this system of equations have no solution?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $3$. The lines are parallel (no solution) when the coefficients are proportional: $\frac{18}{6}=\frac{k}{1} \Rightarrow k=3$ (and the constants are not in that same ratio).

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the honeybee apiary, a theater sold $29$ tickets for a total of USD $310$. Adult tickets cost USD $16$ and child tickets cost USD $9$. How many adult tickets were sold?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $7$. Let $a$ = adult tickets. $16a+9(29-a)=310 \Rightarrow 7a=49 \Rightarrow a=7$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the local farmers market, $\begin{cases}6x-3y=0\\5x-6y=28\end{cases}$ What is the value of $x$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $-4$. Solving the system by elimination gives $x=-4$ and $y=-8$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the performing arts academy, the real number $t$ satisfies $\frac{23t + 20}{2} = 391 + \frac{20}{2}$. What is the linear expression $p = 23t - 20$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $762$. Multiplying by 2 gives $23t = 782$, so $23t - 20 = 782 - 20 = 762$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the coastal aquarium, the linear system $17t + 6y = 284$ and $34t + (p + 6)y = 578$ has no solution. What is the constant parameter $p$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $6$. A linear system has no solution when the lines are parallel and distinct: $\frac{34}{17} = \frac{p + 6}{6} \implies p = 6$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the public transit depot, $\begin{cases}3x+y=2\\6x+ky=14\end{cases}$ For what value of $k$ does this system of equations have no solution?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $2$. The lines are parallel (no solution) when the coefficients are proportional: $\frac{6}{3}=\frac{k}{1} \Rightarrow k=2$ (and the constants are not in that same ratio).

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the wildlife sanctuary, the ordered pair $(t, y)$ satisfies $t + y = 26$ and $17t + 3y = 302$. What is the coordinate $t$ in $p(t, y)$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $16$. Substituting $y = 26 - t$ into $17t + 3y = 302$ yields $t = 16$.

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Challenging Synthesis (15–20)

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the historic lighthouse, if the linear equation $6(x + 4) = 6x + c$ has infinitely many solutions for $x$, what is the value of the constant $c$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $24$. Expanding the left side gives $6x + 24 = 6x + c$. For the equation to hold for all real $x$, the constant terms must be equal, so $c = 24$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: At the botanical conservatory, adult tickets sell for USD $5$ each and student tickets sell for USD $8$ each. On Saturday, a total of $18$ of these items were sold for a combined revenue of USD $114$. How many adult tickets were sold on Saturday?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $10$. Let $a$ be the number of adult tickets and $b$ be the number of student tickets. Then $a + b = 18$ and $5a + 8b = 114$. Substituting $b = 18 - a$ gives $5a + 8(18 - a) = 114 \implies -3a = -30 \implies a = 10$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In the system of linear equations $3x + 4y = 11$ and $9x + ky = 26$ modeling two supply lines at the municipal library, $k$ is a constant. If the system has no solution, what is the value of $k$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $12$. A system of two linear equations has no solution when the lines are parallel and have different $y$-intercepts. Multiplying the first equation's $x$-coefficient by $3$ gives $9$, so $k = 4 \times 3 = 12$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: For the community theater inventory model, the equation $\frac{1}{2}x + 4 = \frac{42}{6}$ relates the reserve count $x$ to the target quota. What is the value of $x$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $6$. Multiply both sides of the equation by $6$: $3x + 24 = 42 \implies 3x = 18 \implies x = 6.$

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: For a calibration balance at the regional bakery, if the linear equation $6(x + 7) = 6x + c$ has infinitely many solutions for $x$, what is the value of the constant $c$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $42$. Expanding the left side gives $6x + 42 = 6x + c$. For the equation to hold for all real $x$, the constant terms must be equal, so $c = 42$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: At the coastal aquarium, oak saplings sell for USD $9$ each and maple saplings sell for USD $12$ each. On Saturday, a total of $24$ of these items were sold for a combined revenue of USD $246$. How many oak saplings were sold on Saturday?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $14$. Let $a$ be the number of oak saplings and $b$ be the number of maple saplings. Then $a + b = 24$ and $9a + 12b = 246$. Substituting $b = 24 - a$ gives $9a + 12(24 - a) = 246 \implies -3a = -42 \implies a = 14$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Intermediate Application (29–37)

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the wildlife sanctuary, a store sells notebooks for USD 3 each and pens for USD 1.50 each. Maria spent USD 18 on a total of 8 items. How many notebooks did she buy?
questions.answer: Let $n$ = notebooks: $3n+1.5(8-n)=18 \Rightarrow 1.5n=6 \Rightarrow n=4$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the charter ferry service, in the plane, the line $14x + 15y = 210$ intersects the axes at points $A$ and $B$. What is the sum of intercepts $f$ of $14x + 15y = 210$?
questions.answer: The intercepts are $15$ and $14$, whose sum is $15 + 14 = 29$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the textile workshop, in a calculation for the community orchard (case 44), what is the sum of all solutions to the equation $|2x-10| = 4$?

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the geology lab, the ordered pair $(x, y)$ satisfies $x + y = 16$ and $20x + 4y = 240$. What is the coordinate $x$ in $f(x, y)$?
questions.answer: Substituting $y = 16 - x$ into $20x + 4y = 240$ yields $x = 11$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the carpentry workshop, in the coordinate plane, consider the lines $f(x) = 6x - 14$ and $g(x) = 76$. What is the intersection coordinate $x$ where $f(x) = g(x)$?
questions.answer: Setting $6x - 14 = 76$ yields $6x = 90 \implies x = 15$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the historic lighthouse, $\begin{cases}6x+6y=-8\\12x+ky=-7\end{cases}$ For what value of $k$ does this system of equations have no solution?
questions.answer: The lines are parallel (no solution) when the coefficients are proportional: $\frac{12}{6}=\frac{k}{6} \Rightarrow k=12$ (and the constants are not in that same ratio).

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the community orchard, the point $A(19, 14)$ lies on the line $fx - 4y = 134$. What is the coefficient $f$?
questions.answer: Substituting $(19, 14)$ gives $19f = 190 \implies f = 10$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the environmental club, a linear function $p(t)$ satisfies $p(0) = 9$ and $p(7) = 58$. What is the input $t$ for which $p(t) = 100$?
questions.answer: The slope is $m = 7$, so $p(t) = 7t + 9$. Setting $7t + 9 = 100$ gives $t = 13$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the neighborhood hardware store, $\begin{cases}6x-6y=54\\2x+3y=-2\end{cases}$ What is the value of $x - y$?
questions.answer: Solving the system by elimination gives $x=5$ and $y=-4$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the honeybee apiary, in the system of linear equations $2x + 7y = 35$ and $6x + ky = 50$, $k$ is a constant. If the system has no solution, what is the value of $k$?
questions.answer: A system of two linear equations has no solution when the lines are parallel and have different $y$-intercepts. Multiplying the first equation's $x$-coefficient by $3$ gives $6$, so $k = 7 \times 3 = 21$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the carpentry workshop, for the textile workshop inventory model, the equation $\frac{1}{2}x + 7 = \frac{87}{6}$ relates the reserve count $x$ to the target quota. What is the value of $x$?
questions.answer: Multiply both sides of the equation by $6$: $3x + 42 = 87 \implies 3x = 45 \implies x = 15.$

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations
questions.q: In a model for the community orchard, at the geology lab, soccer balls sell for USD $9$ each and training cones sell for USD $12$ each. On Saturday, a total of $26$ of these items were sold for a combined revenue of USD $270$. How many soccer balls were sold on Saturday?
questions.answer: Let $a$ be the number of soccer balls and $b$ be the number of training cones. Then $a + b = 26$ and $9a + 12b = 270$. Substituting $b = 26 - a$ gives $9a + 12(26 - a) = 270 \implies -3a = -42 \implies a = 14$.

questions.target: Linear Equations in One Variable & Systems of Equations

questions.answer: A system of two linear equations has no solution when the lines are parallel and have different $y$-intercepts. Multiplying the first equation's $x$-coefficient by $3$ gives $18$, so $k = 4 \times 3 = 12$.
